notes: The section a diff cannot produce at all, so the eval is mostly about the searching. Presence of an affected-but-unchanged list is mechanical and lives in checks/blast-radius.sh; whether the entries are RIGHT is the product and is judged here.

cases.expected_output: A blast-radius diagram reaching from the new column to the unchanged query that scopes the selectable list, two lists side by side, a reading order with reasons, and a statement of which of the five files carry design.
expectations: app/queries/active_projects.rb is in the affected list with a why clause, and the search that found it is written down

At least one empty search is recorded as a search — an unrecorded absence cannot be told from an omission, and this diff has real ones (no other caller of archive!, no other reader of the archived scope)
The dashed nodes in the diagram are exactly the unchanged-and-affected ones, and the solid ones exactly the changed ones
The reading order puts the migration and schema before the code that reads the column, and each why is a reason rather than a restatement of the filename
Where the attention goes distinguishes the files carrying design from db/schema.rb, which is generated output — and ranks without excusing anything from coverage
The slug uniqueness validation appears as secondary work in a neutral register: independently reviewable, no criticism of the author for bundling it

cases.expected_output: A blast radius that crosses the boundary: the new column and the serialized field on one side, the hand-written type and the unchanged picker query on the other.
expectations: web/src/queries/selectableProjects.ts is in the affected list with the reason it is affected, and the search that found it is recorded
Affected code is found on both sides of the boundary, not only in api/ — a section that searched one side and stopped is the failure this fixture is built to catch
The diagram crosses the boundary rather than stopping at the serializer, and marks the unchanged client consumers as unchanged
The reading order follows dependency rather than directory: it does not read all of api/ and then all of web/ when the interesting pair is the serializer and the type
Rung 3 is stated once and correctly — a remote exists but the head is unpushed, so citations are plain text — without repeating the explanation at each citation
Nothing in the section grades the change, scores it, or recommends a decision
